subject: Incident follow-up: technical synopsis and remediation register
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Christine Nguyen <christine.nguyen@clearwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Incident follow-up: technical synopsis and remediation register

Hi Christine,

Thanks again for your patience while we finished the initial investigation into Monday's inference degradation affecting your production tenant. Attached you'll find a short diagnostic summary (executive + technical), an event timeline, and a remediation register that lists proposed fixes, owners, and target dates.

High-level summary:
- What happened: A confluence of an autoscaling race on the batch router and a kernel selection regression for the quantized transformer path resulted in intermittent token-generation stalls for ~14 minutes during peak traffic.
- Impact on ClearWave: elevated tail latency and an increased error rate for ~3% of requests during the window; some long-running requests saw token gaps.
- What we did: rolled back the kernel selector, applied a targeted throttle to the router, and validated KV-cache integrity for your affected model versions.

Action items (full list in remediation-register-20261110.xlsx):
1) Kernel selector patch (Hannah) — short-term patch live within 24 hours; longer-term unit tests for selection safety due in 2 weeks.
2) Autoscale policy change (Jonas) — update to cooldowns and backoff tuning by EOD Wednesday.
3) Customer verification plan (Marissa / ClearWave) — smoke tests and a focused traffic replay; we propose a scheduled window (see calendar link).

I've attached the files and included a link to the collaborative doc for step-by-step verification. If you'd like, we can run through the timeline and each remediation item in a 30-minute call; I've proposed a slot on Wed, Nov 11 (link below).

Attachments: diagnostic-summary-20261110.pdf, event-timeline-20261110.csv, remediation-register-20261110.xlsx

Next steps: please confirm whether Wed 11:00 AM PT works for you to review the verification plan.

Thanks,
Irene

Hi Christine — answers inline below and in the attached diagnostic summary.

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 6:05 PM Christine Nguyen <christine.nguyen@clearwave.com> wrote:
> - Can you confirm whether any customer data was dropped or returned incomplete during the token gaps?

Short answer: no customer data loss.
Details: the issue caused late token emission and, in some cases, truncated streaming chunks for long-lived streams. We validated application-level payload integrity for requests routed to your tenant: all completed requests either returned full payloads or returned a clear error (no silent data corruption). The diagnostic-summary includes hashes and a sample verification set we ran against your production logs.

> - Is the kernel selector fix a rollback only or a code change? Maintenance window?

We performed an emergency rollback of the selector to the prior vetted release to stop the immediate stalls (already done). The remediation-register lists a code change with improved selection heuristics and additional unit/integration tests; that will be a code release with normal release controls and a brief maintenance notice if the longer-term patch is promoted to dedicated clusters. Short-term rollback requires no customer maintenance window.

> - Outline the verification traffic replay

Planned verification: a deterministic replay of representative traffic (non-production identifiers) for 30 minutes against a canary instance, then a 15-minute observation window. We will provide a small test harness and a pre-built set of requests that match your peak patterns. Marissa will coordinate the replay schedule with your ops team; the proposed slot on Wed 11:00 AM PT is on the calendar link in the original message.

Meeting invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=clearwave-20261111-review
Pre-read doc: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/clearwave/incident-20261110

Action owners (from remediation register):
- Hannah Schmitt — short-term kernel selector patch and unit tests (owner).
- Jonas Weber — autoscale policy tuning + verification of backoff behavior.
- Marissa Cole — customer coordination + replay execution.

We will circulate iteration notes in the shared doc and close items as we verify. See attachments for technical traces and the sample verification set.

Thanks — will join the call at 11.
Irene

Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
